Uhniv Jewish Cemetery

Jewish Cemetery · Lviv Oblast, Ukraine

Not demolished. This record contains a contradiction worth flagging: it is categorized as demolished and overbuilt, yet the source's demolished field marks it as 'no.' Uhniv's Jewish community, documented from as early as 1550, became independent from the kehila of nearby Zhovkva by the late 18th century, and Belz Hasidism — one of the largest Hasidic dynasties in the world today — became popular locally by the mid-19th century. The Zionist leader Avigdor Spitzer maintained a Hebrew-language school in his own house. In late July 1942, about 1,000 Jews were deported to the Bełżec extermination camp, and the remaining population was confined to the Rava-Ruska ghetto, documented elsewhere in this collection, that September.
